notes.f1: Not recovered -- the tree names "R.C. Spriggs" and "Jennie Cross" as parents (stub persons I1/I2), not John William Spriggs. The fixture's own notes say this is directly attested by the 1910/1920 US Census via record_search, but record_search was WAF-blocked on every attempt this entire run (three parameter shapes tried, all rejected) -- an environment/infrastructure failure, not an agent capability gap. The agent correctly recognized the block, logged it, and pivoted to fulltext_search, which does not cover 1900/1910 census content -- it said so explicitly in the exhaustive-search summary. image_transcribe/image_read were also blocked all run (no OpenRouter key configured), so it couldn't read the one WWI draft card or obituary image that might have named a parent directly either. Under those two blockers it produced a genuinely careful, well-documented "probable"-tier proof (30+ logged searches, three independent corroborating sources, honest tier justification, explicit acknowledgment that the highest-value record type was inaccessible) -- proof_quality_score reflects that soundness independent of the miss. But it is a probable conclusion about a different family entirely: Grand Forks County marriage/naturalization records and two later biographical compilations, versus the fixture's Iowa-born father / Norway-born mother in Beadle County -- no overlap in names, origins, or even the county the family is placed in. Not a recall or reasoning failure so much as a tool-availability failure that steered the whole research path away from the one collection that would have answered it directly.
notes.f2: Not recovered -- same root cause as f1. The mother the tree identifies (Jennie Cross) has no attested Norway origin or any connection to Charlotte Marie Westby; the identification rests on the same WAF-blocked-record_search/inaccessible-image chain of indirect evidence described in f1's note, not on any record naming her as Reuben's mother.
